claims.text: Fully spin-polarized DFT augmented with many-body corrections can accurately predict ferromagnetic ground states in transition-metal compounds.
DFT+DMFT and advanced hybrid exchange-correlation functionals are examples of methods that provide relevant many-body corrections.
Improved treatment of nonlocal exchange and dynamic electron correlation is critical for stabilizing magnetic order.
Some transition-metal compounds exhibit ambiguous or incorrect magnetic ordering in standard or non-spin-polarized DFT calculations.
At zero temperature, the balance of exchange-correlation and electron-interaction energies determines ground-state magnetic ordering.
Enhanced exchange-correlation functionals and many-body corrections improve the treatment of nonlocal exchange and dynamic electron correlations.
The augmented method represents spin-polarization and electron-interaction energy contributions more accurately than methods neglecting these effects.
More accurate representation of spin-polarization and electron-interaction energies stabilizes and enables clear identification of a ferromagnetic ground state.
The augmented method will yield a lower total energy for the ferromagnetic configuration than for alternative magnetic or non-magnetic configurations.
A lower total energy for the ferromagnetic configuration identifies ferromagnetism as the predicted ground state.
Non-spin-polarized or standard DFT calculations often fail to capture exchange-correlation and dynamic-electron effects.
Failure to capture exchange-correlation and dynamic-electron effects can produce ambiguous or incorrect predictions of ground-state magnetism.
The augmented approach is expected to be most effective in systems with significant local electron correlation and spin polarization.
The augmented approach may have limited applicability in weakly correlated or highly delocalized materials.
The quantitative improvement in predictive accuracy may vary among materials.
